title: A bounded frequency search finds no clear departure from the GJ 674 second orbital harmonic in 224 HARPS exposures
abstract: We test whether the second GJ 674 velocity wave has a frequency different from twice the known planet frequency. In 224 public HARPS-RVBank version 02 exposures from five seasons, a 1201-point frequency search within plus or minus 0.001 cycles per day improves weighted squared error by only 0.0644, or 0.040 percent. Nine full-search conditional residual sign tests give tail fractions from 0.768 to 0.816. At 1.697 m/s amplitude, specified frequency offsets of 0.25 cycles across the observing span have 84 to 88 percent recovery in four phase trials under one conditional noise rule. The result gives no clear departure from the exact harmonic in this bounded test. It does not prove eccentricity or exclude a second planet near exact 2:1. The model uses fixed periods, simple seasonal activity terms and unverified noise assumptions. The data share spectra with prior work. No new planet or independent instrument confirmation is found. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, input hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: A bounded second-wave frequency profile and nine conditional full-search tail fractions. Zero frequency offset is the exact orbital harmonic. The noise tests give no clear departure.
